manifest.name: Word Documents
manifest.description: Read Word .docx files: convert to Markdown with headings and tables intact, pull just the outline, or extract tables as structured rows.

capabilities.name: Document to Markdown
capabilities.description: Convert a .docx to Markdown, preserving headings, lists and tables.

capabilities.name: Document outline
capabilities.description: Return only the heading structure, to locate a section cheaply.

capabilities.name: Extract tables
capabilities.description: Extract every table as structured rows.

capabilities.name: Working with Word documents
capabilities.description: How to read and reason about .docx files, including a dependency-free fallback when the plugin's own tools are unavailable.

manifest.name: Git
manifest.description: Git and forge workflow, end to end: search issues on the remote, branch before fixing, keep commits reviewable, open a pull request, and land it. Plus the judgment parts — rebase-or-merge, conflict resolution, finding the change that caused a bug, and getting work back after a bad command.

needs.prompt: Personal access token for the code host, with issue and pull-request scope
API base URL — leave blank for github.com, set it for a self-hosted or enterprise instance

capabilities.name: Fixing an issue end to end
capabilities.description: The full path from a reported issue to a branch: finding and reading the issue, deriving a branch name, and the rule that a fix never starts on the base branch.

capabilities.name: Opening and landing pull requests
capabilities.description: Turning a finished branch into a reviewable pull request and getting it merged — what the description owes a reviewer, which merge strategy to use, and the checks that must pass before anything lands.

capabilities.name: Writing commits
capabilities.description: How to stage and split work into commits that survive review and stay bisectable — what belongs in one commit, what a message has to explain, and when to amend rather than add.

capabilities.name: Branching, rebasing and conflicts
capabilities.description: When to rebase and when to merge, how to update a branch without rewriting shared history, and how to resolve conflicts by understanding both sides rather than picking one.

capabilities.name: Investigating history
capabilities.description: Finding the commit that introduced a behaviour: searching history by content rather than by message, reading blame past reformatting, and driving bisect with a script instead of by hand.

capabilities.name: Recovering lost work
capabilities.description: What is recoverable after a bad command and what is not — reflog, the three reset modes, dangling commits, and the small set of operations that genuinely destroy data.

capabilities.name: Sharing work safely
capabilities.description: Remotes, force-push safety, and the rules for rewriting history other people may already have — including how to tell whether a branch is genuinely private.

capabilities.name: Fix an issue
capabilities.description: Take an issue, branch, fix it, verify it, and open a pull request that closes it.

capabilities.name: Investigate a regression
capabilities.description: Find the commit that introduced a bug, using a scripted bisect over a reproducer rather than reading diffs by hand.

capabilities.name: Prepare a branch for review
capabilities.description: Get the current branch into a state a reviewer can actually read: coherent commits, current with the base, no stray files.

capabilities.name: Explain how this got here
capabilities.description: Reconstruct why a file or function looks the way it does, from the commits that shaped it.

capabilities.name: Issue scout
capabilities.description: Searches the remote's issues for ones matching a description and returns a shortlist with evidence. Delegate so that pages of issue listings do not fill the main conversation.

capabilities.name: History investigator
capabilities.description: Searches history to answer a specific question and returns findings only. Delegate so that dozens of log, blame and diff outputs do not fill the main conversation.

capabilities.name: Conflict resolver
capabilities.description: Works through a conflicted merge or rebase file by file, reading both sides before choosing. Delegate when a conflict is large enough that the hunks would crowd out everything else.

capabilities.name: Search issues
capabilities.description: Search the remote repository's issues by text, label, state and author, returning matches with number, title and status.

capabilities.name: Read an issue
capabilities.description: Fetch one issue in full — body, labels, linked pull requests and comment thread.

capabilities.name: Open a pull request
capabilities.description: Open a pull request from the current branch, with title, description and draft state.

capabilities.name: Pull request status
capabilities.description: Report a pull request's review state, required checks and mergeability, to decide whether it can land.

capabilities.name: Merge a pull request
capabilities.description: Merge an approved pull request with the repository's merge strategy, and delete the source branch. Refuses while required checks are failing or unfinished.

capabilities.name: users.history.list
capabilities.description: Lists the history of all changes to the given mailbox. History results are returned in chronological order (increasing `historyId`). For more information, see [Synchronize clients with Gmail](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/sync). (GET /gmail/v1/users/me/history)

historyTypes.description: History types to be returned by the function

maxResults.description: Maximum number of history records to return. This field defaults to 100. The maximum allowed value for this field is 500. Defaults to "100".

pageToken.description: Page token to retrieve a specific page of results in the list.

labelId.description: Only return messages with a label matching the ID.

startHistoryId.description: Required. Returns history records after the specified `startHistoryId`. The supplied `startHistoryId` should be obtained from the `historyId` of a message, thread, or previous `list` response. History IDs increase chronologically but are not contiguous with random gaps in between valid IDs. Supplying an invalid or out of date `startHistoryId` typically returns an `HTTP 404` error code. A `historyId` is typically valid for at least a week, but in some rare circumstances may be valid for only a few hours. If you receive an `HTTP 404` error response, your application should perform a full sync. If you receive no `nextPageToken` in the response, there are no updates to retrieve and you can store the returned `historyId` for a future request.

capabilities.name: users.messages.import
capabilities.description: Imports a message into only this user's mailbox, with standard email delivery scanning and classification similar to receiving via SMTP. Note that the maximum size of the message is 150 MB. (POST /gmail/v1/users/me/messages/import)

processForCalendar.description: Process calendar invites in the email and add any extracted meetings to the Google Calendar for this user. Defaults to "false".

neverMarkSpam.description: Ignore the Gmail spam classifier decision and never mark this email as SPAM in the mailbox. Defaults to "false".

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.identities.create
capabilities.description: Creates and configures a client-side encryption identity that's authorized to send mail from the user account. Google publishes the S/MIME certificate to a shared domain-wide directory so that people within a Google Workspace organization can encrypt and send mail to the identity. For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (POST /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/identities)

body.description: The CseIdentity resource for this request, as the Gmail API defines it.

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.identities.delete
capabilities.description: Deletes a client-side encryption identity. The authenticated user can no longer use the identity to send encrypted messages. You cannot restore the identity after you delete it. Instead, use the CreateCseIdentity method to create another identity with the same configuration. For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (DELETE /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/identities/{cseEmailAddress})

cseEmailAddress.description: The primary email address associated with the client-side encryption identity configuration that's removed.

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.identities.get
capabilities.description: Retrieves a client-side encryption identity configuration. For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (GET /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/identities/{cseEmailAddress})

cseEmailAddress.description: The primary email address associated with the client-side encryption identity configuration that's retrieved.

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.identities.list
capabilities.description: Lists the client-side encrypted identities for an authenticated user. For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (GET /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/identities)

pageSize.description: The number of identities to return. If not provided, the page size will default to 20 entries. Defaults to "20".

pageToken.description: Pagination token indicating which page of identities to return. If the token is not supplied, then the API will return the first page of results.

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.identities.patch
capabilities.description: Associates a different key pair with an existing client-side encryption identity. The updated key pair must validate against Google's [S/MIME certificate profiles](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7300887). For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (PATCH /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/identities/{emailAddress})

emailAddress.description: The email address of the client-side encryption identity to update.

body.description: The CseIdentity resource for this request, as the Gmail API defines it.

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.keypairs.create
capabilities.description: Creates and uploads a client-side encryption S/MIME public key certificate chain and private key metadata for the authenticated user. For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (POST /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/keypairs)

chainValidation.description: The type of certificate chain validation to perform at creation. The request will be rejected if the uploaded chain fails to satisfy the requested validation checks. When unspecified, this parameter defaults to `all`. Defaults to "all".

body.description: The CseKeyPair resource for this request, as the Gmail API defines it.

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.keypairs.disable
capabilities.description: Turns off a client-side encryption key pair. The authenticated user can no longer use the key pair to decrypt incoming CSE message texts or sign outgoing CSE mail. To regain access, use the EnableCseKeyPair to turn on the key pair. After 30 days, you can permanently delete the key pair by using the ObliterateCseKeyPair method. For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (POST /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/keypairs/{keyPairId}:disable)

keyPairId.description: The identifier of the key pair to turn off.

body.description: The DisableCseKeyPairRequest resource for this request, as the Gmail API defines it.

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.keypairs.enable
capabilities.description: Turns on a client-side encryption key pair that was turned off. The key pair becomes active again for any associated client-side encryption identities. For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (POST /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/keypairs/{keyPairId}:enable)

keyPairId.description: The identifier of the key pair to turn on.

body.description: The EnableCseKeyPairRequest resource for this request, as the Gmail API defines it.

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.keypairs.get
capabilities.description: Retrieves an existing client-side encryption key pair. For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (GET /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/keypairs/{keyPairId})

keyPairId.description: The identifier of the key pair to retrieve.

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.keypairs.list
capabilities.description: Lists client-side encryption key pairs for an authenticated user. For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (GET /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/keypairs)

pageSize.description: The number of key pairs to return. If not provided, the page size will default to 20 entries. Defaults to "20".

capabilities.name: users.settings.cse.keypairs.obliterate
capabilities.description: Deletes a client-side encryption key pair permanently and immediately. You can only permanently delete key pairs that have been turned off for more than 30 days. To turn off a key pair, use the DisableCseKeyPair method. Gmail can't restore or decrypt any messages that were encrypted by an obliterated key. Authenticated users and Google Workspace administrators lose access to reading the encrypted messages. For administrators managing identities and keypairs for users in their organization, requests require authorization with a [service account](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount) that has [domain-wide delegation authority](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/OAuth2ServiceAccount#delegatingauthority) to impersonate users with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic` scope. For users managing their own identities and keypairs, requests require [hardware key encryption](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14153163) turned on and configured. (POST /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/cse/keypairs/{keyPairId}:obliterate)

keyPairId.description: The identifier of the key pair to obliterate.

body.description: The ObliterateCseKeyPairRequest resource for this request, as the Gmail API defines it.

capabilities.name: users.settings.delegates.create
capabilities.description: Adds a delegate with its verification status set directly to `accepted`, without sending any verification email. The delegate user must be a member of the same Google Workspace organization as the delegator user. For more information, see [Manage delegates](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/delegate_settings). Gmail imposes limitations on the number of delegates and delegators each user in a Google Workspace organization can have. These limits depend on your organization, but in general each user can have up to 25 delegates and up to 10 delegators. A delegate user must be referred to by their primary email address, and not an email alias. When a new delegate is created, there may be up to a one minute delay before the new delegate is available for use. This method is only available to service account clients that have been delegated domain-wide authority. (POST /gmail/v1/users/me/settings/delegates)
